scenes.title: A parameterized program, made visible
scenes.description: Change the input or parameters. Play the forward trace. Playing moves values through the operations; it does not update the parameters.

nodes.text: FORWARD · VALUES FLOW, PARAMETERS STAY PUT
The result changes. The parameter buffer changes only if another operation writes it.

cues.text: Read the input and the current parameter values.
Multiplication creates the intermediate value w × x.
Add the bias to obtain the prediction. No optimizer ran.

accessibility.text: Compute prediction = w times x plus b. The initial example gives 2 times 3 plus 1 = 7. Forward evaluation computes values; it does not change w or b.

reducedMotion.description: Compute prediction = w times x plus b. The initial example gives 2 times 3 plus 1 = 7. Forward evaluation computes values; it does not change w or b.

scenes.title: Forward, backward, then update
scenes.description: One training example has x = 2 and target = 4. The loss is half the squared error. Adjust w and the learning rate, then play exactly one proposed update.

nodes.text: new w = old w − learning rate × gradient
The moving point shows the proposed update; playing does not commit repeated training steps.
It does not keep training the model.

cues.text: Forward computes the prediction and loss using the starting weight.
Backward computes the gradient. It has not changed w.
The proposed optimizer update subtracts learning rate times gradient.

accessibility.text: For x=2 and target=4, loss=(2w−4)²/2 and gradient=(2w−4)×2. The optimizer proposes new w=w−rate×gradient. At w=0, rate=0.1, loss=8, gradient=−8 and new w=0.8. A large learning rate can overshoot and increase loss.

reducedMotion.description: For x=2 and target=4, loss=(2w−4)²/2 and gradient=(2w−4)×2. The optimizer proposes new w=w−rate×gradient. At w=0, rate=0.1, loss=8, gradient=−8 and new w=0.8. A large learning rate can overshoot and increase loss.

scenes.title: A view changes the map, not the buffer
scenes.description: Select a logical row and column. Toggle a transpose view and watch the same twelve values move. An invalid logical coordinate is reported instead of indexing memory.

nodes.text: A transpose view changes shape and strides. It does not allocate twelve new values.
The view changes shape and strides.

cues.text: The values are one flat allocation. Shape and strides define a view.
Changing the view does not copy the underlying values.

accessibility.text: A 3×4 row-major FP32 tensor has strides (4,1). Logical (row,column) maps to element offset row×4+column and byte offset four times that. The transposed 4×3 view uses strides (1,4), with the same 48-byte allocation. Out-of-range coordinates are invalid.

reducedMotion.description: A 3×4 row-major FP32 tensor has strides (4,1). Logical (row,column) maps to element offset row×4+column and byte offset four times that. The transposed 4×3 view uses strides (1,4), with the same 48-byte allocation. Out-of-range coordinates are invalid.
